text:
jamal: quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a proposal to wire per-tenant dynamic budgets into the policy engine so routing can do admission control + graceful degrade. raising questions before I turn it into a formal PR.

alex: +1 on the concept. we already throttle at ingress for some tenants but not tied to cost/budget. curious how you want to represent budgets (tokens vs windows) and how strict admission should be. :thinking:

jamal: thinking tokens with leak/regen semantics per tenant and per-route multipliers. basic config example: 
```
policy: tenant_budget
  window: 1m
  tokens: 10000
  leak_rate: 167/s
  route_multiplier:
    chat: 1.0
    embed: 0.5
  fallback: degrade_to_cpu_variant
```
This lets policy evals check reservation before queuing.

maria: two high-level concerns: fairness between tenants when capacity tight, and billing vs actual consumption mismatch (users expect budget to map to cost). we need transparent metrics per-tenant + alerting.

chris: implementation note — we should avoid strong global coordination. propose per-replica approximate counters with occasional reconciliation. reservation should be transactional locally: reserve -> enqueue -> decrement async. if reservation fails, short-circuit with degrade or queue-shed.

liza: caution: per-replica approximations can starve a tenant on a different replica. can we use a lightweight global lease service for headroom checks? e.g., cheap tokens from a central allocator only when crossing a local threshold. keeps common-case local but protects at global scale.

alex: agree with hybrid: local fast path + central refills. also suggest a soft/ hard mode: soft lets requests through but annotates and enforces downstream cost limiting, hard denies entry. soft mode helps avoid hard outages for noisy tenants.

jamal: good point. operationally I'd like three outcomes from policy eval: ALLOW (fast-path), DEGRADE (route to cheaper model/quantized variant), or REJECT. and a fallback policy chain.

maria: add: expose tenant burn-rate dashboards and a historical replay tool (we should be able to run past traffic through the new budget logic offline to estimate impact). without that teams will be surprised.

chris: replay tool idea: capture request metadata (tenant, route, tokens_est) and feed into a simulator that applies token accounting. we already have sim infra for routing; can extend it.

liza: what about multi-tenant routes (shared capacity pools)? e.g., free-tier and enterprise share a pool sometimes. do budgets become labels on pools instead of tenants?

jamal: design notes:
- default: tenant-level budget with optional pool binding.
- route multipliers let us express cost differences.
- policy engine API: evaluate_budget(tenant_id, route, tokens_est) -> {decision, reason, remaining_tokens_est}
- metrics: per-tenant token_consumed_total, burn_rate, rejected_count, degrade_count.

alex: runtime complexity: we will need fast tagging in the router so a) cost_est is accurate pre-queue and b) we can short-circuit before KV-cache hits. small CPU overhead but saves GPU time in rejects.

maria: +1 to adding an opt-in migration mode: start in monitoring-only (decisions simulated, not enforced) for 2 weeks per customer before flipping to soft then hard.

sre-bot: deploy-notes: plan canary rollout: 5% tenants monitoring-only -> 1% soft mode -> 0.5% hard mode, with automatic rollback on error-rate increase > 0.5% or latency p95 increase > 10%.

chris: action items I can take: prototype local counter + central lease refiller, and hook into sim infra for replay. estimate 2 sprints.

liza: I'll mock the API surface for evaluate_budget and the config schema; want to align with existing policy DSL.

jamal: I'll write the RFC PR with config examples, telemetry requirements, and the canary plan. target for RFC merge: next Thu.

alex: one more: add a developer-facing error + reason codes so owners know why requests were degraded (budget_exhausted, rate_limited, policy_error). helps SLOs and debugging.

maria: thanks — this addresses my concerns. +1 to replay/monitoring-first.

jamal: cool, thanks everyone. I'll post the draft RFC link once up. :rocket:
